html:
Kim Jong Il was the ruler of North Korea from his father's death in 1994 until his own in 2011. Soviet records show he was born in 1941 in the Soviet Far East; official history places his birth on Mount Paektu in Korea.

His father Kim Il Sung groomed him for decades, the first hereditary succession in a communist state. He ran propaganda and the arts, and he loved film so much that he had a South Korean director and actress kidnapped in 1978 to make films for him.

His first years in power saw the famine of the 1990s, in which hundreds of thousands died. He ruled through the army under a military-first policy and pushed the nuclear programme to the first test in 2006. He held a summit with South Korea's Kim Dae-jung in 2000. His son Kim Jong Un succeeded him.
